cards.explanation: The answer is "She is my sister." That's what Abraham says of his wife Sarah while he's staying in Gerar (Genesis 20:2). Four little words, and this chapter is off and running. Abimelech, king of Gerar, is about to hear them, and I think things are about to get complicated for him.

The answer is that Abimelech has Sarah brought to him. Abimelech, the king of Gerar, had Sarah brought to him (Genesis 20:2). The text says it plainly and moves on. That's one of those moments where you lean toward the page and say, uh oh.

The answer is married. God tells Abimelech, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman.” (Genesis 20:3) That's a heavy thing to hear, even in a dream. I bet Abimelech's eyes were wide open the whole time he was asleep.
The answer is True. Abimelech says, “Lord, would You destroy a nation even though it is innocent?” (Genesis 20:4) He doesn't just sit there quietly. He answers God right in the middle of the dream.

The answer is “He is my brother.” Abimelech says Sarah herself said those words (Genesis 20:5). So both of them told him the same thing, and he points to that as part of his defense. Honestly, he's got his paperwork in order.
The answer is True. God tells him, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience…” (Genesis 20:6) God doesn't brush off what Abimelech said. He answers him directly, still in the dream.

The answer is that God did not let him. God says it Himself: “That is why I did not let you touch her.” (Genesis 20:6) He also says He kept Abimelech from sinning against Him. So the stopping was God's doing, start to finish.

The answers are prophet and pray, friends. God tells Abimelech, “…for he is a prophet; he will pray for you and you will live.” (Genesis 20:7) Notice who is getting called a prophet: Abraham, the same man who just got caught in a mess. God still names him that, and God still has him pray for the king. The prayer is how Abimelech lives. And later in the chapter, Abraham does exactly that (Genesis 20:17).

The answer is False. It isn't only Abimelech. God says, “…be aware that you will surely die—you and all who belong to you.” (Genesis 20:7) The warning covers his whole household, and that's a big reason to listen.

The answer is terrified. The text says the men were terrified (Genesis 20:8). Abimelech tells them all that happened, and they don't take it lightly. I think a boss telling you his dream shouldn't normally scare you, but this one did.

The answer is guilt. Abimelech says Abraham has brought “…such tremendous guilt upon me and my kingdom?” (Genesis 20:9) He's talking about his whole kingdom, not just himself. That's a lot of weight to carry out of a dream.

The answer is fear. Abraham says, “Surely there is no fear of God in this place.” (Genesis 20:11) That's what he tells Abimelech he thought to himself. He follows it with, “They will kill me on account of my wife.” (Genesis 20:11) So the worry he names is about his own life.

The answer is that they would kill him because of his wife. Abraham says he thought, “They will kill me on account of my wife.” (Genesis 20:11) That's his reason, in his own words. He tells Abimelech straight out.

The answer is False, friends. It's flipped. Abraham says, “…she really is my sister, the daughter of my father—though not the daughter of my mother—and she became my wife.” (Genesis 20:12) So she's his father's daughter, not his mother's.

The answer is loyalty, bakers. Abraham tells the king what he asked of Sarah: “This is how you can show your loyalty to me…” (Genesis 20:13) He's explaining himself after the fact, and he ties it back to when God had him journey from his father's house. Explaining yourself after the fact is a skill I know well, friends. I've done it over a tray of crumbs.

The answer is True. The text says Abimelech brought “…sheep and cattle, menservants and maidservants…” and gave them to Abraham (Genesis 20:14). He restored Sarah too. That's quite a gift on top of giving his wife back.

The answer is “Settle wherever you please.” Abimelech says, “Look, my land is before you. Settle wherever you please.” (Genesis 20:15) That's a wide-open invitation from a king. It comes right after he gives Abraham sheep, cattle and servants and restores Sarah to him (Genesis 20:14).

The answer is that she is completely cleared. Abimelech tells Sarah, “It is your vindication before all who are with you; you are completely cleared.” (Genesis 20:16) The silver comes with those words. He says it right to her.

The answer is that the LORD closed all the wombs. The text says the LORD “…had completely closed all the wombs in Abimelech’s household.” on account of Sarah (Genesis 20:18). That's why they needed healing after Abraham prayed (Genesis 20:17). It's a heavy detail, so I'll just say it plainly and leave it there.
